other_failure_modes.description: When computing aggregated features (like daily family or store means) to create lags, the agent filters out the test set before the aggregation. As a result, the aggregated dataframe lacks entries for the test dates, so when merged back into the main dataset, the lagged features become entirely NaN for the test set, severely harming predictive performance.

other_failure_modes.name: row_based_shift_on_missing_dates
other_failure_modes.description: The agent applies a direct `.shift(16)` on grouped rows to compute a 16-day lag. This assumes that every single day is present in the dataset. If dates are missing (e.g., store closures on holidays like Christmas), a row-based shift will incorrectly shift across the missing days, resulting in a lag of more than 16 days.

summary: The agent implements a solid baseline with proper time-based validation, log transformation, and tree-based modeling. However, it introduces a critical feature engineering bug: by filtering out test data before creating date-aggregated lag features, those features end up entirely missing (NaN) during test inference. Additionally, it relies on row-based shifting which is brittle to missing dates, and it evaluates its stochastic model only once.
